A political controversy has emerged in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir following the deaths of two Special Police Officers whose bullet-riddled bodies were found in the Dachhan forest area of Kishtwar on November 12. Rashpal Kumar, 45, and Babi Chand, 57, had gone missing a day earlier along with their service rifles. While security officials initially blamed militants, Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee president Tariq Hamid Karra demanded an impartial investigation into potential mistaken identity by the Indian Army.

According to Karra, local reports suggest the two officers went hunting in civilian clothes with firearms on November 11. They reportedly passed two army checkpoints without issues while traveling to the area, but may have been misidentified as militants by military personnel upon their return, a risk possibly compounded by a change in security duty shifts. Karra emphasized that all theories, including militant involvement and accidental shooting, must be thoroughly probed.

Meanwhile, local Bharatiya Janata Party MLA Shagun Parihar criticized authorities over the handling of the victims' remains, expressing outrage that the bodies were transported to their homes in a dumper truck with perceived indignity.

The incident has sparked conflicting narratives between security assessments and local political leaders, underscoring demands for transparency and proper protocol observance.

stories.title: Pakistan and Sri Lanka eye series victory in Rawalpindi Test match
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Sri Lanka will square off in the second and final Test of their series at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi on Tuesday, with both teams looking to experiment since neither has much at stake regarding World Test Championship standings. The opening Test at the same venue ended in a draw after being disrupted by bad weather and overcast conditions that favored fast bowlers.

During the first Test, Pakistan handed debuts to four players, with Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha, and Arafat Minhas scoring solid fifties, while 31-year-old pacer Saqib Khan claimed 7-130 in Sri Lanka's first innings. However, Razaullah struggled significantly and is expected to be replaced by young fast bowler Ali Shabbir from Rahim Yar Khan. Saud Shakeel proved to be a standout performer for Pakistan, scoring 93 and 97 to rescue the hosts from potential defeat. Meanwhile, premier batsman Salman Ali Agha will seek to end his personal lean patch.

Sri Lanka put on a strong batting display in the previous match, featuring a record fifth-wicket partnership between Dhananjaya de Silva, who scored 167, and captain Kusal Mendis, who made 119. The visitors aim to strengthen their bowling attack to conclude their month-and-a-half-long tour on a positive note, having previously lost the T20I series 2-1 and the ODI tri-series final to Pakistan.

Pakistan bowling coach Shaun Tait noted that the Rawalpindi pitch features some grass cover and should offer helpful conditions for fast bowlers who maintain disciplined line and length. Tait defended his pace attack's performance in the first Test, expressing satisfaction with their spells. Pakistan's probable squad for the match includes Babar Azam as captain, alongside key players like Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Abbas, and Saqib Khan.

stories.title: US Air Travel Recovers Gradually Following Nationwide Ground Stop Disruption
stories.summary:
US air travel began slowly returning to normal after a three-day nationwide disruption caused by a rare no-takeoff order issued by aviation authorities. Triggered by a faulty upgrade to air traffic control communication cables, the Friday afternoon ground stop marked only the second time US airspace was grounded nationwide since the 9/11 attacks, stranding millions of passengers.

By Monday morning, flight tracking data showed 250 cancellations and over 700 delays for US-related flights, representing a substantial improvement from Sunday's figures of more than 2,300 cancellations and 10,000 delays. President Donald Trump blamed the Federal Aviation Administration debacle on the previous administration led by Joe Biden, while arguing that Congress must approve funds to overhaul outdated infrastructure. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted that clearing the backlog of misplaced planes and crews would take until Tuesday to fully resolve, while defending his role and appealing for $50 billion to modernize 1960s-era radar and equipment.

The massive travel chaos highlighted vulnerabilities in aging American aviation technology, reigniting political debates between Republicans and Democrats over federal funding and infrastructure management.

stories.title: Copper Hits Four-Month Low Amid Dollar Strength and AI Worries
stories.summary:
Copper prices dropped to their lowest point in more than four months on the London Metal Exchange, declining 0.9% to $13,280 a metric ton by 1100 GMT after touching $13,210.5, a level not seen since July 8. The downward movement was attributed by SP Angel analyst John Meyer to an AI-driven sell-off, potential delays in data center rollouts, a stronger US dollar, and weaker economic data from China.

The metal has experienced a 10% decrease since reaching a record high in September during an AI-driven investment wave, which was fueled by the Democrats' victory in US midterms and complicated by the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Recent sessions pushed copper's Relative Strength Index to 30, signaling oversold conditions for the first time since March. Meanwhile, sluggish Chinese factory production and consumption contrasted with strong import demand, keeping the Yangshan premium near $290 a ton and reducing Shanghai Futures Exchange inventories by 18%.

The US dollar maintained April 2025 highs as investors awaited statements from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh regarding interest rates, making dollar-priced metals costlier for international buyers. Other London Metal Exchange materials also fell, with aluminium down 1.0% to $2,980, zinc dropping 0.5% to $3,692, lead easing 0.6% to $1,882.50, nickel slipping 0.2% to $15,950, and tin losing 0.8% to $46,270.

stories.title: Pakistani Rupee Edges Higher While Global Currencies and Oil Fluctuate
stories.summary:
The Pakistani rupee registered a marginal gain of 0.01% against the US dollar in the inter-bank market, closing at 276.57 with an appreciation of Re0.03. This followed a previous week where the local unit gained 0.02%, moving from 276.66 to 276.60 according to State Bank of Pakistan data. The slight upward trend comes as currency and commodity markets react to broader international economic indicators and central bank policies.

Globally, the Japanese yen traded near two-month lows at 159.69 against the dollar and 176.04 against the euro, following news that Japan's third-quarter economy contracted by an annualized 0.1%. The US dollar index climbed to 103.44, its highest level since April 2025, driven by hawkish Federal Reserve remarks and a hot October inflation report. Markets are pricing a 93.9% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the upcoming Federal Reserve meeting ending on December 9.

Meanwhile, oil prices declined amid expectations of a supply surplus, influenced by nearly restored Middle East shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and reduced Chinese refinery throughput in October. Brent futures dropped 0.6% to $95.30 a barrel, and US West Texas Intermediate fell 0.3% to $88.34, impacting overall currency parity indicators.

stories.title: Karachi Flour Prices Rise Again as Grain Costs Burden Citizens
stories.summary:
Flour mill owners in Karachi have implemented another price hike across various flour categories, worsening the financial strain on inflation-weary residents and raising concerns over access to basic foods like bread and naan. Mills raised standard flour by Rs. 6 per kilogram and fine flour by Rs. 12 per kilogram last week.

Following the increase, wholesale and retail rates have surged significantly. Standard flour is priced at Rs. 163 per kilogram wholesale and Rs. 170 retail, while fine flour reaches Rs. 183 wholesale and Rs. 190 retail. Branded chakki flour costs Rs. 200 wholesale and between Rs. 220 and Rs. 230 retail, with branded flour matching that retail range.

Mill owners attribute the adjustments to open market wheat trading at Rs. 147 per kilogram, making it unsustainable to purchase expensive grain while keeping flour prices low. The continuous price escalations have intensified public frustration over mounting inflation and the daily challenge of managing household budgets for staple goods.

stories.title: Islamabad Court Grants Four-Day Remand for Suspects in Girl's Death
stories.summary:
A judicial magistrate in Islamabad approved a four-day physical remand for a woman and a seminary teacher connected to the death of a 13-year-old girl who allegedly suffered violence at a Federal Investigation Agency director's residence. Police brought the suspects before Judicial Magistrate Naima Iffat at the district and sessions court, requesting an eight-day remand for further interrogation.

The court ultimately granted a four-day physical remand after initially reserving its decision. The arrests followed a first information report registered at the Shams Colony police station under Section 302 of the Pakistan Penal Code, initiated by a complaint from the victim's father.

The complainant, a resident of Rahim Yar Khan, stated that his daughter was a seminary student living with close relatives in the Police Lines Headquarters in Islamabad's sector H-11. He was informed that she suddenly fell ill, was taken to a hospital, and died, prompting him to seek a murder investigation after discovering signs of torture on her body.

stories.title: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina Withdraws From Spain's Davis Cup Squad
stories.summary:
Spanish tennis player Alejandro Davidovich Fokina has withdrawn from the upcoming Davis Cup Final 8 tournament. The world number 16 chose to conclude his physically demanding season ahead of schedule to focus on healing for the year 2027.

Davidovich explained via social media that recurring physical struggles and injuries required multiple breaks throughout the year, noting that his physical condition needs additional recovery time prior to competing again. Daniel Merida will step in to take his place on the roster.

Spain's strong lineup for the tournament also features Carlos Alcaraz, Rafael Jodar, Pedro Martinez, and Marcel Granollers. The team is scheduled to play against Austria during the quarter-final round of the competition.

The Davis Cup Final 8 event is set to occur on indoor hardcourts located at the SuperTennis Arena in Bologna, Italy, running from November 24 through November 29. Additional match-ups feature defending champions Italy playing South Korea, the Czech Republic meeting Canada, and Great Britain facing Germany.

stories.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Retreat From Recent Gains on High Inventories
stories.summary:
Malaysian palm oil futures experienced a decline on Monday, bringing an end to a three-session winning streak. Persistent high domestic stockpiles continued to exert downward pressure on market valuations, while anticipated decreases in production helped limit the extent of the losses.

At the close of trading, the benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange dropped 18 ringgit, translating to a 0.39% decrease, to settle at 4,547 ringgit, which equals $1,111.74 per metric ton. David Ng, a proprietary trader at Iceberg X Sdn Bhd, noted that the market traded cautiously as forecasted slower output for November offered support, while large inventories weighed on overall sentiment.

Cargo surveyors reported that shipments of Malaysian palm oil products between November 1 and November 15 decreased by 1% to 3.9% relative to the previous month. Meanwhile, crude oil prices declined amid indications of recovering oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, which reinforced expectations of surplus supply despite fresh tanker incidents threatening Middle East exports. Weaker crude oil futures reduce the appeal of palm oil as a feedstock for biodiesel.

In related markets, Dalian's most-active soyoil contract dropped 0.07%, its palm oil contract gained 0.27%, and Chicago Board of Trade soyoil prices fell 0.56%. Additionally, the ringgit weakened by 0.2% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly more affordable for buyers utilizing foreign currencies, while India's October palm oil imports increased approximately 7% month-on-month to reach 874,740 metric tons, according to the Solvent Extractors’ Association of India.

stories.title: Belgium's All-Time Top Scorer Romelu Lukaku Retires From International Soccer
stories.summary:
Romelu Lukaku, the all-time leading goalscorer for Belgium, announced his retirement from international competition on Monday. His departure concludes a 16-year career representing his country, during which he netted 94 goals across 135 appearances.

The 33-year-old striker stands as the fifth-highest goalscorer in the history of men's international football. His international career highlights include helping Belgium secure a third-place finish at the 2018 World Cup, which marked the most successful era in the national team's history.

Expressing gratitude on Instagram, Lukaku stated that he gave everything to the national team, experienced every possible emotion, and appreciated the support of his teammates and coaches. During his tenure, he competed in four World Cups and three European Championships, describing the journey as an amazing and enjoyable ride.

Lukaku was an unused substitute during Belgium's 4-1 home victory against Italy in the Nations League on Sunday. At the club level, he started his career with Anderlecht before playing for teams such as Chelsea, Everton, Manchester United, and Inter Milan, and he currently plays for the Turkish club Fenerbahce.

stories.title: Zafar Masud's Tenure as Bank of Punjab President Extended Through 2030
stories.summary:
The Bank of Punjab has formally extended the employment contract of Zafar Masud to continue serving as its President and Chief Executive Officer. The decision was finalized following approval from the bank's Board of Directors and an official notification issued by the Punjab Finance Department.

The extension will secure Masud's leadership position for an additional three-year term starting from April 16, 2027. The Board of Directors authorized the contract prolongation during their 339th emergent meeting, which took place on November 16, 2026, concurrently with the issuance of the provincial finance department's notification.

Alongside his executive duties at the Bank of Punjab, Masud has also held prominent leadership roles within the broader financial sector. He was elected as the Chairman of the Pakistan Banks’ Association initially in March 2024, succeeding Muhammad Aurangzeb, and secured the position again in December 2025 after previously serving as the organization's Senior Vice Chairman.

Throughout his professional tenure, Masud has actively emphasized the banking sector's financial contributions to the economy of Pakistan. He previously reported that the banking industry contributed Rs 1.6 trillion to the national exchequer in 2024, a total that encompassed Rs 856 billion in direct corporate and income taxes, Rs 63 billion in sales and excise duties, and over Rs 685 billion in withholding tax.

stories.title: U.S. Prosecutors Link Indian Employee to Alleged Pakistan Assassination Plot
stories.summary:
U.S. prosecutors have connected an employee of the Indian government, Vikash Yadav, to a separate alleged plot targeting a Sikh leader in Pakistan. This revelation emerged through court documents filed in the case of Nikhil Gupta, who entered a guilty plea for participating in a conspiracy to murder Sikh activist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun within the United States. Federal prosecutors are recommending a prison term of 293 months, equating to 24 years and five months, for Gupta. A sentencing memorandum submitted by the Justice Department outlines coordinated efforts in May 2023 between Gupta and Yadav to locate and eliminate a target inside Pakistan.

According to the court filing, Gupta messaged Yadav in May 2023 to report that operatives dispatched to Pakistan had arrived and were actively searching for the intended target. Prosecutors state that Yadav requested regular updates and instructed Gupta to supply the operatives with extra funds to execute the killing the following day. Furthermore, the documents indicate that Yadav furnished specific location details regarding the target, which Gupta was tasked with relaying to the operatives. On May 14, 2023, Yadav allegedly directed Gupta to have the target killed if captured, warning that another opportunity might not arise. Court papers identify Yadav as a worker in India's Cabinet Secretariat, which oversees the Research and Analysis Wing, the nation's external intelligence agency.

Defense attorneys representing Gupta confirmed in their own court filing that both men discussed a separate potential target located in either Nepal or Pakistan. These allegations concerning Pakistan are distinct from the American assassination plot targeting Pannun, a dual U.S.-Canadian citizen and Sikh separatist leader. Prosecutors characterized the plot against Pannun as an attempted political assassination that threatened U.S. sovereignty and fundamental values. Gupta entered his guilty plea on February 13, 2026, for charges involving conspiracy to assassinate Pannun, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering. U.S. District Judge Victor Marrero is scheduled to sentence Gupta on November 20 in a federal court in New York.

stories.title: China Announces Trilateral Summit for Xi, Trump, and Putin in Shenzhen
stories.summary:
The leaders of China, Russia, and the United States will convene in Shenzhen this week for their first trilateral summit to discuss world peace and strategic stability. Chinese President Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are scheduled to meet on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning announced the meeting on Monday, describing the talks as having ground-breaking significance while noting that Beijing provided limited details on the specific agenda.

Top diplomats from the United States and China previously discussed the possibility of addressing nuclear disarmament during the three-way talks. Washington, aiming to curb China's growing nuclear arsenal, wants Beijing to join a broader nuclear arms control agreement. Beijing maintains that the United States and Russia must first decrease their own massive nuclear stockpiles before entering such negotiations. Following the expiration of a U.S.-Russia bilateral arms treaty in February, Trump urged for a comprehensive new agreement including China, which initially declined. However, Chinese diplomat Wang Yi and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio recently agreed on the significance of leader-level conversations regarding peace and denuclearization.

President Trump also indicated that the leaders will likely address his ongoing war in Iran, noting efforts to end the regional conflict that has disrupted global shipping and raised oil prices. While China has actively sought to mediate the Iranian crisis as a key economic partner, discussions regarding Russia's invasion of Ukraine appear less certain. A recent Wall Street Journal report suggested Putin wanted the summit to broker a favorable peace deal for Moscow, though European leaders and Ukrainian officials have expressed strong apprehension. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that the gathering could resemble a modern redistribution of spheres of influence, potentially sidelining Kyiv and encouraging continued conflict.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drones Strike Kerch Bridge, Causing Minor Damage, Kremlin Says
stories.summary:
Ukrainian drones targeted the Crimea Bridge over the Kerch Strait in an overnight strike, resulting in minor damage according to statements from the Kremlin and regional authorities. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed during a press briefing that minor damages are currently being assessed and that traffic across the bridge remains operational. Sergei Aksyonov, the Russia-backed governor of Crimea, previously stated that traffic restrictions would remain in place until approximately midday.

The 19-kilometer Crimea Bridge serves as the sole direct transport link connecting Russia to the Crimean peninsula, which was annexed by Russia from Ukraine in 2014. The infrastructure project has historically functioned as a vital supply route for Russian military forces operating in Ukraine and stands as one of President Vladimir Putin's prominent engineering achievements. The bridge features separate roadway and railway sections supported by concrete stilts, alongside a wider span held by steel arches to allow maritime passage between the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

Since the initiation of the Russian invasion in February 2022, the bridge has faced multiple attacks by Ukraine, including an October 2022 truck bombing that killed four individuals and restricted its capacity for several months. This latest overnight drone strike follows an escalation of Russian attacks against bridges within Ukraine, including strikes in the capital city of Kyiv. While international recognition of Crimea as part of the Russian Federation remains limited, the Kremlin maintains that the territorial status of the peninsula is permanently settled.

stories.title: Israeli Opposition Leaders Denounce Netanyahu Over Alleged Election Plot
stories.summary:
Israeli opposition leaders condemned an attempted coup on Monday following press reports indicating that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office attempted to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party prior to last month's election. Yair Lapid, who led the previous legislature's opposition and co-chairs the Beyachad list, wrote on social media that the revelations point to an attempted coup rather than mere election disruption. According to an investigative report by Israel’s Channel 12, Netanyahu's chief of staff, Ido Norden, contacted police on the eve of the October 27 election to lodge a complaint against members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.

Norden reportedly directed police toward a former employee of Netanyahu's office acting as an intelligence source, whose information subsequently led to the arrest of three Raam members. Authorities later released the three men after determining the allegations were entirely unfounded. Following the incident, Netanyahu publicly accused Arab political parties of electoral fraud after they secured a record number of seats in Parliament. The Likud party subsequently issued a formal statement denying all allegations linking them to the plot.

Additional reports from the Israeli newspaper Haaretz indicated that David Zini, head of the domestic security service Shin Bet, requested permission to wiretap leaders of the Joint List, another Arab slate, but the attorney general rejected the request due to insufficient evidence. Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen joined in denouncing the actions as a criminal mechanism designed to rig election results from the highest levels of government. Raam's second-in-command, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an immediate independent criminal investigation to hold all responsible parties accountable. Meanwhile, Netanyahu's primary rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, asserted that the caretaker prime minister could no longer remain in power. Neither Netanyahu's political bloc nor Eisenkot's opposition secured the 61 seats necessary to form a government, leaving both Arab parties positioned to support Eisenkot.

stories.title: IGI Investments Secures Approval to Evaluate Stake in Nimir Resins
stories.summary:
IGI Investments (Private) Limited has secured in-principle approval from its Board of Directors to examine the acquisition of up to a 60% stake in Nimir Resins Limited. The parent organization, IGI Holdings Limited, announced this prospective development via a formal notice submitted to the Pakistan Stock Exchange on Monday following a board meeting held on November 16, 2026.

Under the proposed initiative, the ownership share would be acquired from several existing substantial shareholders, namely Rudolf Pakistan (Private) Limited, Zafar Mahmood, Khalid Qazi, Imran Afzal, Umar Iqbal, and Aamir Jamil. However, the potential transaction remains contingent upon several critical conditions, including the outcome of satisfactory due diligence, the establishment of a final transaction structure, and successful negotiations concerning the purchase price.

Additional requirements for the deal involve executing a definitive agreement, satisfying all relevant legal frameworks, and securing necessary corporate and regulatory approvals. Nimir Resins Limited itself has a long history, originating as a public limited company in Pakistan in 1964 before undergoing conversion in 1991. The enterprise focuses on manufacturing various industrial components, such as coating resins, composite resins, optical brighteners, textile auxiliaries, and paper surface sizing agents.

Statistical data from June 30, 2025, shows that Nimir Resins maintains 141.32 million outstanding shares distributed among 5,093 shareholders. Related parties, associated companies, and undertakings control the majority share at 45.45%, while the local general public accounts for the remaining 32.91% holding stake in the organization.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court Seeks Police Report on Missing Russian Citizen
stories.summary:
The Peshawar High Court in Pakistan held a hearing on Monday regarding a habeas corpus petition concerning a Russian national who has allegedly gone missing within the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region. Chief Justice S.M. Ateeq Shah presided over the session and directed the local police department to submit a comprehensive official case report within a fourteen-day timeframe.

During the proceedings, the petitioner's legal counsel detailed that the missing individual, Ali Glegov, initially arrived in Islamabad before traveling onwards to Peshawar, where he subsequently vanished. The bench questioned the evidentiary basis establishing that the disappearance occurred locally, prompting the lawyer to explain that both police authorities and the Russian embassy confirmed Glegov reached Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and has remained untraced since February 28.

The lawyer further noted that the missing persons commission declined to hear the matter due to the absence of an official identity card. When the court inquired about the purpose of Glegov's arrival, the counsel responded that he traveled specifically to meet acquaintances he had established through social media platforms.

Concluding the session, the high court ordered law enforcement officials to provide complete call detail record data alongside the requested investigation report. The bench then officially adjourned the proceedings to await the submission of the required police documentation.

stories.title: Belgium Forward Romelu Lukaku Announces Retirement from International Football
stories.summary:
Belgium striker Romelu Lukaku announced his retirement from international football on Monday, concluding a 16-year career with the national team where he established himself as his country's record goalscorer with 94 goals across 135 appearances. The 33-year-old forward, who currently plays club football for Turkish side Fenerbahce, stated that he feels completely at peace with his decision to step away from international competition.

Throughout his career with the Red Devils, Lukaku participated in four World Cups, helping the team achieve a third-place finish at the 2018 tournament and reaching the quarter-finals of the recent tournament before a defeat to Spain. He made his senior international debut as a teenager in 2010 and was an unused substitute during Sunday's 4-1 UEFA Nations League victory over Italy. Expressing his gratitude on social media, the former Chelsea, Manchester United, and Inter Milan player thanked fans, teammates, and coaches for their unwavering support throughout the journey.

Tributes poured in from former teammates and sports officials following the announcement. Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois and midfielder Axel Witsel shared words of appreciation for the shared memories, while Belgium technical director and former Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet praised Lukaku's leadership qualities and essential presence in the dressing room. The Belgian football association confirmed they fully respect his choice.

Belgium will play their first match without Lukaku in March during the upcoming Nations League quarter-finals. Technical staff emphasized that the national squad must now look forward and direct its full focus toward future preparations and ongoing team development in international play.

stories.title: Imran Khan Sends Detailed Letter to Chief Justice Highlighting Custody Concerns
stories.summary:
Founder of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Imran Khan transmitted a comprehensive letter addressed to the Chief Justice of Pakistan, Justice Yahya Afridi, and all judges of the apex judiciary. Delivered via Barrister Salman Safdar, the correspondence stems from a three-hour legal consultation at Adiala Jail and outlines grave grievances regarding his detention conditions, health status, alleged rights violations, and the non-enforcement of Supreme Court directives.

The document details that the former prime minister has been subjected to solitary confinement for 22 hours daily since December 20, 2025, cut off from human contact and outside communication. Legal consultations revealed that he has suffered an 85 percent loss of vision in his right eye and has only been permitted four lawyer visits over the past year, causing severe psychological strain.

The letter additionally raises serious health concerns regarding his wife, Bushra Bibi, noting her detention conditions mirror his own and that she received complicated surgery for a retina problem diagnosed in April 2026. The correspondence alleges that prison authorities have withheld her medical treatment records, blocked telephone calls from his sons Qasim and Suleiman, and arbitrarily suspended weekly family visits without valid justification.

Emphasizing persistent government non-compliance, the communication recalls an August 18 court order mandating his transfer to Shifa International Hospital, the formation of a medical board featuring cardiologists and ophthalmologists, and the authorization of weekly family visits alongside bi-weekly phone calls to his sons. The letter concludes with an urgent appeal to the Chief Justice to intervene and enforce compliance with fundamental prisoner rights and mandated medical care.

stories.title: CyberCube Estimates Microsoft 365 Outage Insured Losses Below $100 Million
stories.summary:
Cyber risk analytics firm CyberCube announced on Monday that global insured losses stemming from the recent Microsoft 365 outage will likely stay under $100 million. The company established a conservative upper limit of $350 million and stated the incident will have a loss ratio impact of zero to two percent for cyber insurers. This assessment maintains the Level 2 moderate rating previously issued to clients on November 13.

The global disruption originated from a failure in Microsoft Exchange Online, which impacts Outlook email and affected users across more than 70 countries. Core services for Teams, SharePoint, Copilot, and Microsoft security tools also experienced degraded functions because they rely on Exchange Online. Microsoft explained that a network-capacity upgrade caused the technical issue rather than a cyberattack. Severe disruption lasted approximately 18 hours, while the broader incident continued for about 38 hours.

Jon Laux, CyberCube’s vice president of products and analytics, noted that several elements will suppress insured losses despite the length of the event. Insurance policies typically only respond when coverage extends business interruption to non-malicious system failures at external providers. Additionally, analysts observed widespread utilization of alternative communication channels alongside an absence of data theft, data corruption, or material revenue loss reports.

CyberCube formulated its financial estimate by utilizing its catastrophe model and global industry exposure database, which aligns with Marsh Re’s perspective of a minimal insurance market effect. In contrast, Kovrr co-founder and chief product officer Shalom Bublil offered a preliminary projection on Friday suggesting insured losses could approach $700 million. CyberCube indicated it will review its figures if significant new details emerge.

stories.title: عمران خان کا چیف جسٹسز کو خط، اہلیہ سمیت طبی سہولیات کا مطالبہ
stories.summary:
راولپنڈی کی اڈیالہ جیل میں قید سابق وزیرِ اعظم عمران خان نے سپریم کورٹ، وفاقی آئینی عدالت اور اسلام آباد ہائی کورٹ کے چیف جسٹس صاحبان کو اپنے وکیل سلمان صفدر کے ذریعے ایک خط ارسال کیا ہے۔ اس خط میں انھوں نے اور ان کی اہلیہ بشریٰ بی بی کی صحت کو درپیش شدید خطرات کا ذکر کرتے ہوئے فوری طبی امداد اور ہسپتال منتقلی کی اپیل کی ہے۔ عمران خان کا مؤقف ہے کہ وہ زندہ رہیں گے تبھی اپنی بے گناہی ثابت کر سکیں گے۔

خط میں دعویٰ کیا گیا ہے کہ سابق وزیرِ اعظم کو روزانہ بائیس گھنٹے قیدِ تنہائی میں رکھا جاتا ہے اور انہیں اہل خانہ، وکلا، کتب اور ٹیلی ویژن تک رسائی حاصل نہیں۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ دائیں آنکھ کی پچاسی فیصد بینائی ختم ہو چکی ہے اور قید تنہائی کی وجہ سے ان کا بلڈ پریشر خطرناک حد تک بڑھ کر 192 اور 193 تک پہنچ گیا ہے، جس سے برین ہیمرج اور دل کے دورے کا خطرہ ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ انہوں نے بشریٰ بی بی کی خراب صحت اور آنکھ کی پیچیدہ سرجری کا بھی حوالہ دیا۔

دوسری جانب وفاقی وزیر پارلیمانی امور طارق فضل چوہدری نے ان الزامات کو حقائق کے منافی اور ریلیف حاصل کرنے کی کوشش قرار دیا ہے۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ عمران خان کو جیل میں تمام ضروری طبی سہولیات فراہم کی جا رہی ہیں اور ڈاکٹروں نے ان کی صحت کو تسلی بخش قرار دیا ہے۔ حکومت کا مؤقف ہے کہ سابق وزیرِ اعظم کو قانون کے مطابق سزا دی گئی ہے اور ان کے علاج میں کوئی کوتاہی نہیں برتی گئی۔

ادھر بشریٰ بی بی کے وکلا نے بھی اسلام آباد ہائی کورٹ میں ان کی ہسپتال منتقلی کی درخواست دائر کی ہے، جس میں جیل کے کمرے میں صفائی کے ناقص انتظامات اور حشرات کی موجودگی کا شکوہ کیا گیا ہے۔ عمران خان نے اپنی اپیل میں عدالتوں سے مطالبہ کیا ہے کہ سپریم کورٹ کے اٹھارہ اگست کے حکم پر عمل درآمد کیا جائے اور انہیں قانون کے مطابق مناسب طبی سہولیات دی جائیں۔

stories.title: Pakistani Prime Minister Calls for Regional Security and Cooperation at ECO Meeting
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif urged regional nations to unite against security threats during the 30th session of the Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers in Islamabad. Emphasizing dispute resolution via dialogue, his remarks coincided with Pakistan assuming the ECO chairmanship for the 2026–2027 term under the theme "Revitalising Regional Cooperation for a Strong and Resilient ECO."

During the gathering, delegates welcomed the adoption of the Islamabad Declaration alongside strategic economic objectives spanning 2026 to 2035. Prime Minister Shehbaz highlighted priorities such as expanding trade, enhancing transport connectivity, and fostering sustainable development to integrate landlocked member states with international markets using Pakistani ports including Karachi, Port Qasim, and Gwadar.

The discussions occurred alongside broader geopolitical tensions, including strains involving Afghanistan and the wider US-Iran conflict. Islamabad aims to use its two-year leadership tenure to overcome infrastructural and bureaucratic barriers, boost regional transit, and invite international partners to events marking Lahore as the ECO Tourism Capital for 2027.

The meeting underscores Pakistan's ongoing diplomatic balancing act as it seeks to maintain open communication channels and serve as a regional trade conduit despite persistent regional security hurdles and challenges to economic integration.

stories.title: Hindustan Zinc Plans $8.5 Billion Investment to Double Capacity
stories.summary:
India-based Hindustan Zinc revealed plans on Monday to invest approximately 800 billion rupees, equivalent to $8.50 billion, over the next three to five years. The capital expenditure aims to nearly double the company's metal production capacity as leadership positions the business to capitalize on rising demand across the infrastructure and steel sectors. Funding for the massive expansion will rely on a combination of internal accruals and debt.

The strategic initiative targets an increase in total production capacity to 2 million tonnes per annum, up from the current 1.1 million tonnes per annum. Domestic demand for zinc is projected to double over the next five to 10 years, even though tight mine supply and project delays continue to constrain overall smelter output. Hindustan Zinc recorded a capacity utilization rate of approximately 92% during the financial year that ended in March 2026.

Specific operational additions include 765,000 tonnes per annum of new zinc smelting capacity and 200,000 tonnes per annum of lead smelting capacity, bringing those segments to the targeted 2 million tonnes per annum aggregate. Furthermore, the company intends to expand its silver refining capacity by 700 tonnes per annum. These expansions come shortly after the company reported a twofold increase in quarterly profit last month, driven by higher zinc prices fueled by global supply constraints and projected deficits.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Closes Higher as Inflows Offset Global Pressures
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee finished Monday's trading session stronger, outpacing most regional peers as a resurgence in foreign equity inflows and supportive policy measures helped steady the currency. One-month realized volatility dropped to roughly 4%, down from 6% two weeks earlier. The currency opened largely flat before appreciating due to dollar sales by foreign banks, likely tied to custodial flows, and private banks acting on behalf of corporate clients.

Throughout the session, the rupee advanced to close 0.3% higher at 93.9225 against the US dollar. India’s benchmark Nifty 50 stock index rose 0.6%, benefiting from limited exposure to crowded artificial intelligence trades that have drawn intense investor scrutiny throughout November. Conversely, MSCI’s broader gauge of Asian equities dropped more than 2%, dragged down by negative performances in South Korea and Taiwan.

Radhika Rao, senior economist and executive director at DBS Bank, highlighted that foreign equity purchases reached a record monthly high of nearly $10 billion for November, representing a dramatic turnaround from prior outflows, while debt segments experienced modest and consistent inflows. These robust capital flows protected the rupee against shifting expectations for faster Federal Reserve interest rate hikes and ongoing fluctuations in oil prices.

Market attention later shifted to comments from Fed leader Kevin Warsh for insights regarding future borrowing costs in the United States. According to the CME FedWatch tool, interest rate futures have fully priced in a rate hike for the following month, with an 8% probability assigned to a larger 50 basis point increase.

stories.title: US Vice President JD Vance Remains Undecided Regarding 2028 Presidential Bid
stories.summary:
United States Vice President JD Vance is currently undecided on whether he will launch a presidential campaign in 2028, according to recent media reports citing anonymous sources. Vance has reportedly discussed the prospective run with his wife, Usha, and other family members, though he is unlikely to reach a final decision until after the New Year and may wait until late spring to make any formal announcements.

Sources close to the vice president noted that he is being cautious to avoid prematurely shifting public attention away from President Donald Trump. Despite recent Republican losses during the midterm elections, allies maintain that Vance remains the party's leading candidate for the upcoming presidential cycle, bolstered by established connections with prominent conservative donors and technology figures such as Peter Thiel, David Sacks, and Elon Musk.

Furthermore, Vance recently met with members of the Rockbridge Network, a conservative donor collective he helped establish, which could potentially back his campaign. His political engagements and relationship-building efforts during the midterm campaigns are expected to provide significant advantages should he ultimately decide to enter the 2028 race.

stories.title: Indian Shares Extend Gains Driven by Foreign Inflows and Commodities
stories.summary:
Indian equity markets advanced on Monday, building upon a three-week winning streak propelled by strong foreign fund inflows and decreasing crude oil prices. The Nifty 50 increased by 0.58% to reach 25,291.10, while the BSE Sensex climbed 0.63% to hit 82,102.85. This upward movement reflects a notable recovery for Indian equities, which underperformed relative to other emerging markets for a significant portion of the preceding two years.

Data from the National Securities Depository indicates that foreign investors have purchased a record net total of $8.9 billion in Indian shares throughout November. This substantial influx has helped reduce their year-to-date outflows to $22.5 billion and brought the benchmark Nifty's losses for 2026 down to under 3.5%. Analysts, including Vikash Kumar Jain of CLSA, point out that recent global anxieties surrounding artificial intelligence have redirected foreign interest toward India, where large-cap stocks offer more attractive and stable valuations.

Market performance was broad-based, with ten out of sixteen major sectors posting gains, though broader small-caps and mid-caps declined by 1.1% and 0.5% respectively. Heavyweight financial sectors performed strongly, with private lenders rising 0.9% to reach a record high, led by HDFC Bank gaining 1.6%. Among individual stocks, Deepak Fertilisers jumped 7.9% following a reported 85% year-on-year surge in quarterly profit, whereas Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles dropped 8.7% after revising its margin outlook for Jaguar Land Rover.

Meanwhile, Brent crude futures experienced a 0.4% decline to settle at $95.4 per barrel. This drop was driven by expectations of an impending supply surplus as commercial shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz from the Middle East recover closer to pre-war volumes, further aiding market sentiment in India.

stories.title: Imran Khan Petitions Chief Justices for Urgent Medical Care in Open Letter
stories.summary:
Incarcerated former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan has issued an open letter to the chief justices of the Federal Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court, and the Islamabad High Court. Shared on social media by his lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar on November 13, the letter outlines severe medical concerns for both Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, while they are held at Adiala jail. Khan stated that he is writing from a solitary cell as his only remaining outlet, detailing a stark decline in his health, including uncontrolled blood pressure spikes reaching 192 and 193 on November 10. Doctors have warned him that he is highly vulnerable to a cardiac arrest and a brain haemorrhage, with his heart already sustaining damage at age 74. 

Khan's correspondence also highlights the critical condition of his wife, Bushra Bibi. According to the letter, she suffered a retinal detachment in April and underwent a secret eye surgery, but now cannot open her eyes or endure light, risking permanent blindness without another procedure. The former premier asserted that their extended isolation and solitary confinement for up to twenty-two hours a day have severely impacted their mental and physical well-being. He noted that Safdar discovered during an authorized visit that Khan had lost 85 percent of the vision in his right eye, a fact allegedly withheld from his family and legal team.

The communication underscores what Khan describes as relentless political victimisation through numerous court appearances and a 17-year sentence in the Toshakhana-2 case concerning an expensive Bulgari jewellery set gifted by the Saudi crown prince in May 2021. He criticized the judicial system for failing to grant him relief or implement a previous Supreme Court order from August 18 mandating his transfer to Shifa International Hospital. Emphasizing that he does not seek favors, Khan implored the judiciary to enforce existing court orders and ensure proper medical treatment, warning that current conditions could prove fatal.

Matters matter because the health and legal standing of a former head of state under strict detention involve significant constitutional and human rights questions in Pakistan. The open letter serves as a direct appeal to the highest judicial authorities to intervene regarding prison conditions and the implementation of medical directives. The case underscores broader tensions surrounding political detentions, access to legal counsel, and the enforcement of judicial mandates within the country's penal system.

stories.title: Pakistan and Turkmenistan Discuss Energy Cooperation and Regional Grid Connectivity
stories.summary:
Turkmenistan’s Minister of Energy, Annageldi Saparov, met with Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Energy, Sardar Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari, in Islamabad to discuss bilateral cooperation in the energy sector and regional grid connectivity. A primary focus of the discussions was the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan (TAP) power transmission project. During the talks, Minister Leghari invited Turkmenistan to join the CASA-1000 project and noted that Pakistan has encouraged Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan to extend the CASA-1000 transmission line to Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. 

Leghari emphasized that future industrial and commercial activities in Gwadar will trigger a major surge in electricity demand, proposing that Iran and Turkmenistan explore enhancing power transmission capacity to the port city through the Iranian grid via a joint expert group. He also suggested converting the CASA-1000 project from a one-way electricity flow system into a two-way flow to enable power exchanges during mutual times of need and enhance financial sustainability. Regarding the TAP project, Leghari pointed out that Pakistan has provided three of the seven required fundamental technical data sets and called for an expedited exchange of technical information and an early meeting of both countries' technical working groups.

Turkmenistan’s Minister of Energy Annageldi Saparov reiterated his country's commitment to completing the TAP power transmission project, which aims to supply electricity to over 300 million people in the region. Saparov noted that Turkmenistan has already completed laying its transmission line up to the Afghan border, with remaining phases and feasibility assessments up to Quetta to be handled by the technical working group. The 1,150-kilometre-long, 500 kV project carries a 1,200 MW capacity.

The engagement matters because both nations are seeking to advance major cross-border energy infrastructure initiatives designed to alleviate power deficits and integrate regional energy markets. Successful execution of projects like TAP and CASA-1000 will directly impact energy security, trade, and economic development across Central and South Asia.

stories.title: Litton Das Scores Century as Bangladesh Posts 400 Against South Africa
stories.summary:
Bangladesh was bowled out for 400 on the second day of the first Test match against South Africa at the Wanderers Stadium. Resuming their innings at 327 for six, the visiting team added 73 runs to their overnight total before losing their remaining four wickets during the morning session. This score marks Bangladesh's highest ever total in Test cricket against South Africa.

Litton Das, who resumed his innings at 92, reached his eighth Test century by hitting a top-edged pull for a six off bowler Marco Jansen. Das went on to score 120 runs before being caught at midwicket off the bowling of Dane Paterson. Paterson was the most effective bowler for South Africa during the morning, claiming all four of the remaining wickets to finish with figures of four wickets for 92 runs.

The innings featured significant contributions from other batsmen, including Tanzid Hasan, who scored 67 runs, and Towhid Hridoy, who contributed 137 runs. Kagiso Rabada also performed strongly for the South African bowling attack, securing five wickets for 70 runs across the innings, which lasted a total of 101.2 overs.

This performance is significant for Bangladesh as it establishes a new benchmark for their highest innings total against South Africa in the longer format of the game. Reaching the 400-run milestone provides the visiting team with a competitive foundation on the scoreboard as the first Test match progresses.

stories.title: Robert Pattinson Officially Cast as the Next James Bond Franchise Star
stories.summary:
Actor Robert Pattinson has been officially cast as the legendary secret agent James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig in the long-running cinematic franchise. Known for his roles in "The Batman" and "The Odyssey," Pattinson takes over the iconic 007 mantle following Craig's departure in the 2021 film "No Time to Die," where the previous iteration of the character met his end.

Speculation regarding the role previously linked several actors to the coveted part, including Jacob Elordi, Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult, Josh O'Connor, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, and Harry Styles. Pattinson's selection follows a commercially successful period that included high-grossing appearances in "The Drama," "Primetime," and "The Odyssey," alongside his ongoing commitment to the Batman film franchise.

Filmmaker Denis Villeneuve has been appointed to direct the upcoming franchise instalment, following Amazon MGM acquiring creative control from longtime producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. The casting signifies a fresh direction for the enduring spy series as production prepares for the next chapter.

stories.title: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina Vows to Return to Bangladesh
stories.summary:
Ousted former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has stated in an email interview with AFP that she intends to return home in December despite facing a threat of death. Hasina, 79, fled to India in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that concluded her 15-year rule. Last year, she was sentenced to death in absentia by a Bangladeshi court after being convicted of crimes against humanity in connection with a deadly crackdown on protesters. 

The announcement follows recent statements from Bangladeshi authorities indicating that she would face execution upon return and has no remaining legal recourse after missing the appeal deadline. Hasina has consistently rejected the legitimacy of the trial. Dhaka has formally requested her extradition from India, a matter that Indian officials state is currently under legal review. Hasina noted that her lawyers have applied for a Bangladeshi passport and national identity card through the high commission in New Delhi to facilitate her homecoming.

Analysts suggest that her declared return is a strategy to maintain political relevance, support her base, and preserve the Awami League party, whose activities are currently banned. Hasina denied allegations that her party was behind recent petrol bomb attacks and asserted she would not request Indian assistance for her travel, emphasizing that extradition is a matter between sovereign states. She also faces over 600 other legal charges, including corruption allegations.

The development matters because Hasina's potential return could significantly impact the political stability and security situation in Bangladesh. Her leadership of the Awami League and the legal implications of her death sentence present major diplomatic and domestic challenges for both Dhaka and New Delhi.

stories.title: Surviving US Army Major Files Whistleblower Complaint Over Deadly Kuwait Strike
stories.summary:
A US Army major who survived an Iranian drone strike in Kuwait has submitted a formal whistleblower complaint alleging that military leadership ignored warnings regarding inadequate troop protection. The attack on March 1 at a makeshift operations centre in Kuwait's Shuaiba port resulted in the deaths of six US Army Reserve soldiers—marking the first American casualties in the war with Iran—and injured dozens of others.

Major Stephen Ramsbottom, who called the incident a tactical failure during a media interview, stated that he repeatedly alerted superiors about the facility's vulnerability to aerial threats. According to the complaint submitted to the House and Senate Armed Services Committees, the site lacked proper fortifications against drones, adequate medical facilities, and functioning early-warning sirens. While senior Pentagon officials previously defended the site's security measures, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth acknowledged that a projectile penetrated the defense systems.

The filing arrives as Democratic lawmakers prepare to launch expansive investigations into the Trump administration's execution of the conflict with Iran when they assume control of Congress in January.

stories.title: Lower Government Borrowing Rates Could Ease Citizen Tax Burdens
stories.summary:
Ordinary citizens and businesses in Pakistan frequently face heavy tax burdens to cover state costs, yet public debt management continues to face scrutiny. With debt servicing consuming 125 percent of Federal Board of Revenue taxes retained by the federal government, 68.5 percent of total revenues, and nearly three times the defense budget, experts argue that avoidable costs should not fall on taxpayers. A major factor in this dynamic involves current accounts, which make up nearly 40 percent of all bank deposits—reaching Rs15.3 trillion by June 2026—on which commercial banks pay no interest. Banks utilize these cheap funds to purchase government securities at exceptionally high returns. Data from the State Bank of Pakistan indicates that banks paid an average interest rate of just 5.53 percent on total deposits in September 2026, while the government borrowed through 12-month treasury bills at 12.79 percent in October 2026, creating a gross difference of 7.26 percentage points.

This gap allows commercial banks to accumulate massive holdings in government securities, totaling Rs40.36 trillion in September 2026, while ordinary taxpayers bear the ultimate cost through levies on petroleum, energy bills, and high income taxes. Applying the gross interest-rate differential yields an estimated annualized figure of approximately Rs2.93 trillion. A proposed legal reform suggests limiting the interest paid to commercial banks on government securities to a reasonable margin of one to two percentage points above average deposit costs. Such a policy could generate annual savings between Rs2,100 billion and Rs2,500 billion, while slightly reducing the State Bank of Pakistan's interest earnings.

Realized savings could be redirected to provide tangible relief to households and struggling entrepreneurs rather than expanding public expenditures. Key proposals include reducing the Petroleum Development Levy and General Sales Tax on electricity bills, doubling the annual income-tax exemption threshold from Rs600,000 to Rs1.2 million for salaried individuals, restoring the Final Tax Regime for exporters at a 2 percent rate, and completely abolishing the super tax while capping corporate income tax at 35 percent. Implementing these changes would help stimulate economic growth, encourage investment, and alleviate poverty by removing excessive taxation on the productive economy.

The author of the proposal is a former federal finance secretary and current chairman of the Policy Research and Advisory Council. Proponents assert that transparency must be maintained by requiring the Ministry of Finance and the State Bank of Pakistan to publish quarterly reports detailing borrowing amounts, interest paid, and actual savings achieved.

stories.title: Federal Constitutional Court Conditionally Permits Peshawar High Court Hearings
stories.summary:
The Federal Constitutional Court modified its earlier directives, conditionally permitting the Peshawar High Court to hear cases concerning the preventive detention of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf workers and activists under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance. Previously, a two-member bench headed by Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan and including Justice Aamer Farooq had barred the Peshawar High Court from hearing these cases on November 5 following the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Under the updated ruling, the high court is allowed to review detention cases on the strict condition that it does not entertain pleas challenging the October 11 proclamation of emergency, governor's rule, or the deployment of the army in aid of civil power.

The legal challenge arose after the Peshawar High Court issued interim orders granting bail to detainees against surety bonds of Rs100,000 each, prompting more than 60 appeals from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Home and Tribal Affairs Department additional chief secretary. Proceedings had initially been suspended under Article 199 and Article 245 of the Constitution, which restrict high court jurisdiction where armed forces operate in aid of civil power. During proceedings, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general submitted a report stating that security threats and terrorist networks across the province remain volatile, making the continued deployment of armed forces indispensable and necessitating the protection of executive security actions from premature judicial interference.

During the hearing, the court also allowed PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and the Peshawar Bar Council to join as parties in the proceedings. Barrister Gohar argued that the initial suspension order severely affected legal practice and left numerous PTI workers and activists detained without a constituted review board. While Justice Farooq observed that a strict literal reading of Article 245 would bring the judicial system to a standstill, the provincial advocate general maintained that review boards for detentions exceeding three months would be established subsequently.

The emergency and governor's rule were initially imposed by the federal government on October 11, citing the provincial government's disengagement from counter-terrorism efforts. This political intervention followed heightened tensions and failed negotiations regarding a planned PTI protest march to Islamabad, resulting in the detention of numerous party members and lawmakers, including non-functional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.

stories.title: Gold and Silver Prices Drop Across Local and International Markets
stories.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan registered a notable decline, following downward movements in the global market. According to rates provided by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the local price of gold per tola decreased by Rs2,000 to settle at Rs408,936 during the day. Similarly, the price of 10-gram gold fell by Rs1,715 to be sold at Rs350,596.

This local correction followed a previous session on Saturday when the per tola gold price had reached Rs410,936 after dropping by Rs700. The domestic reductions directly tracked international trends, where the global rate of gold dropped by $20 to reach $3,864 per ounce.

Precious metals saw broad declines alongside gold. Specifically, the price of silver also experienced a downward adjustment, shedding Rs115 to reach a rate of Rs5,228 per tola in the domestic market.

stories.title: ICC Eliminates Super Six Stage for 2027 ODI World Cup Qualifier
stories.summary:
The International Cricket Council has eliminated the Super Six stage from the 2027 ODI World Cup Qualifier, replacing it with a newly structured knockout format for the upcoming ten-team tournament scheduled for February and March next year. Under the revised layout, the ten participating squads will be split into two groups of five teams each. The top two sides from each group will advance directly to the semi-finals, with the winners meeting in the final match. This modification reduces the total number of matches in the Qualifier from 34 down to 23, marking a clear change from the format utilized across the previous three editions.

The governing body confirmed these adjustments following meetings held in Bali. The qualification pathway leading to the 2027 World Cup has also undergone a comprehensive overhaul approved by the ICC Board in July. The winner of the upcoming Qualifier will secure direct entry into the main 14-team World Cup event. Meanwhile, the teams finishing in second, third, and fourth place will advance to the tournament's first round, designated as the Super Series, where the top-performing side will claim the final remaining berth in the main tournament.

Several teams have already secured their positions in the Qualifier based on their rankings or regional competitions. West Indies and Ireland earned their places through their rankings, while the United States, Netherlands, Scotland, and Oman qualified via Cricket World Cup League 2. The remaining four spots will be decided during the Qualifier Playoff in Nepal next month, which will feature the bottom four teams from League 2 alongside four competitors from the third-tier Challenge League.

stories.title: Jay Shah Elected Unopposed For Second Term As ICC Chair
stories.summary:
Jay Shah has secured another two-year term as the chair of the International Cricket Council after being elected unopposed at the governing body's board meeting held in Bali. The announcement was officially made by the ICC on Monday.

Shah previously made history in 2024 by becoming the youngest person to lead the organization when he assumed the role at the age of 35. Prior to heading the international body, he served as the secretary of the Board of Control for Cricket in India. He is also the son of India's home minister, Amit Shah.

During his upcoming second term, Shah will play a central leadership role in managing cricket's official return to the global sporting stage at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. This milestone marks a significant moment for the administration.

Highlighting the importance of the upcoming Olympic inclusion, Shah emphasized that the event provides an extraordinary platform. He noted it would help introduce the sport to completely new audiences while inspiring an entirely new generation of both players and enthusiastic fans worldwide.

stories.title: Foreign dignitaries gather in Islamabad for the 30th ECO ministerial meeting
stories.summary:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and multiple international delegates arrived in Islamabad to participate in the 30th Economic Cooperation Organisation Council of Ministers meeting. Upon landing, the Iranian foreign minister was welcomed at the airport by Additional Foreign Secretary Muhammad Tariq Wazir and other foreign ministry officials. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar hosted a welcome dinner on Sunday for the visiting foreign ministers and delegation heads, emphasizing close bonds among member states and Pakistan's dedication to regional cooperation, peace, and progress.

Diplomatic activity in the capital began on Saturday with the arrival of Tahsin Ertugruloglu, Foreign Minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. Additional high-level arrivals included Turkey's Deputy Foreign Minister and delegation head Musa Kulaklikaya, Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Deputy Secretary General Ahmad Saidmurodzoda, Organisation of Islamic Cooperation Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, Azerbaijan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Elnur Mammadov, and Kazakhstan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Arman Issagaliyev.

On the sidelines of the summit, Deputy Prime Minister Dar met with ECO Secretary General Dr Asad Majeed Khan. During their discussion, Dar stressed the significance of regional connectivity and economic integration, outlining Pakistan's chairmanship theme, "Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO," and confirming plans to host the ECO Summit in 2027. Dr Khan praised Pakistan's hospitality, arrangements, and coordination for the event.

In a separate meeting, Dar welcomed the OIC secretary general on his maiden visit to Islamabad since taking office. The discussions focused on reinforcing the OIC as a unified voice for the Muslim Ummah. The OIC chief commended Pakistan's diplomatic mediation during the Iran-United States conflict, as well as its active contributions to scientific and technological cooperation through Comstech.

stories.title: Sindh High Court Issues Notices Over Qaim Ali Shah Acquittal Plea
stories.summary:
The Sindh High Court has formally issued notices to the prosecutor general of the National Accountability Bureau and other relevant respondents regarding a review petition filed by former Sindh chief minister Qaim Ali Shah. The court has instructed all respondents to submit their official replies by December 1.

The legal filing follows a previous decision by an accountability court on October 6, which had rejected the former chief minister's initial petition seeking acquittal from the charges brought against him in an ongoing NAB reference case.

In the high court petition, Shah's legal defense argued that the accountability bureau failed to present any verifiable evidence demonstrating monetary benefit or personal corruption related to the executive decisions he made while serving as chief minister.

Furthermore, the petition contended that following the legal amendments enacted in 2022, accountability courts no longer possess the jurisdiction to hear this matter or take punitive action regarding administrative or procedural errors. Consequently, the defense has asked the high court to declare the previous accountability court ruling void and grant full acquittal.

stories.title: Elderly Accident Victim Dies In Karachi Hospital After 20 Days
stories.summary:
An elderly man named Shaheen Baig passed away on Monday while receiving medical treatment in an intensive care unit. He had been battling severe, critical injuries for 20 days following a vehicle collision that occurred near Johar Mor in Karachi on October 17.

The initial accident took place when a car, operated by a clinical psychologist identified as Dr Ayesha Zahid, struck the elderly pedestrian before subsequently colliding with a nearby rickshaw. Funeral prayers for Baig are scheduled to be held at his residence located in Gulistan-e-Jauhar.

In the aftermath of the collision, a chaotic confrontation and heated dispute erupted between the driver and onlookers at the site. Widespread social media attention was drawn to viral video footage depicting the woman arguing, pushing motorcycles, climbing onto vehicle bonnets, and engaging in physical scuffles, which caused major traffic disruptions.

While online speculation questioned whether the driver was intoxicated during the incident, Dr Ayesha strongly denied these claims in a video statement. She explained that she felt unwell due to medication, stepped out to evaluate the damage for potential compensation, and reacted angrily because some of her personal belongings were stolen.

stories.title: میکسیکو میں 40 برس قبل ہونے والا تاریخ کا بدترین گیس دھماکہ
stories.summary:
نومبر 1984 میں میکسیکو سٹی کے مضافاتی قصبے سان خوانیکو میں سرکاری تیل کمپنی پی میکس کے گیس ذخیرہ مرکز پر ایک تباہ کن حادثہ پیش آیا۔ اس المناک واقعے کے نتیجے میں 650 سے زائد افراد لقمہ اجل بنے، আढ़ाई ہزار افراد زخمی ہوئے اور تقریباً 25 ہزار لوگ اپنے گھروں سے محروم ہو گئے۔

حادثے کی صبح گیس کے اخراج سے ایک بڑا بادل بنا جس نے آگ پکڑ لی اور گیس ذخیرہ کرنے والے ٹینکوں میں سلسلہ وار دھماکے شروع ہو گئے۔ اس گیس پلانٹ کے قریب آبادی تیزی سے پھیل چکی تھی اور کچھ گھر تنصیب سے محض 130 میٹر کے فاصلے پر واقع تھے۔ دھماکوں کے نتیجے میں ڈیڑھ کلومیٹر بلند آگ کا ستون آسمان کی طرف اٹھا اور قصبے پر جلتے ہوئے ملبے کی بارش شروع ہو گئی۔

اس وقت چودہ سالہ ورجینیا مارٹینیز اپنے خاندان کے ہمراہ اس علاقے میں مقیم تھیں۔ شدید حرارت، دھوئیں اور خوف کے عالم میں ان کا خاندان پیدل اور اپنی پرانی گاڑی کے ذریعے محفوظ مقام کی طرف نقل مکانی کرنے پر مجبور ہوا۔ اس ہولناک حادثے نے پورے قصبے کو ایک آسیب زدہ اور ویران علاقے میں تبدیل کر دیا تھا جہاں کئی ہفتوں تک عام رسائی ممکن نہ ہو سکی تھی۔

پی میکس نے اس حادثے کی ذمہ داری تسلیم کرتے ہوئے متاثرین کو معاوضہ دینے کا اعلان کیا۔ صحت اور حفاظتی ماہرین کے مطابق یہ سانحہ ناقص شہری منصوبہ بندی، تکنیکی خامیوں اور حفاظتی اصولوں کی سنگین خلاف ورزیوں کا نتیجہ تھا۔ چالیس سال گزرنے کے باوجود اس واقعے کے اثرات اور خوفزدہ کرنے والی یادیں متاثرہ خاندانوں کے ذہنوں میں آج بھی تازہ ہیں۔

stories.title: Bushra Bibi Files Petition Seeking Hospital Transfer Over Health Concerns
stories.summary:
Former first lady Bushra Bibi has filed a fresh petition in the Islamabad High Court through her legal team, Barrister Salman Safdar and Latif Khosa, requesting an immediate transfer from Adiala jail to a specialized medical facility. The filing highlights severe deterioration in her eyesight and warns of the risk of permanent blindness due to inadequate care.

The petition details harsh incarceration conditions, describing her quarters as a large hall-like room with poor sanitation that has resulted in insect infestations. It alleges that bug bites cause painful skin rashes, and notes that jail officials previously killed and removed small snakes from her cell. Medical arrangements at the prison are also criticized, noting that the on-duty doctor is a gynaecologist rather than an eye specialist.

According to the legal filing, Bushra Bibi has been diagnosed with mature cataracts in both eyes and suffers from persistent pain requiring daily painkillers. While doctors previously recommended surgery for November 15, her examination by an ophthalmologist was delayed by seven to eight days. Medical professionals have reportedly warned that post-surgical infections could lead to complete and permanent vision loss, as her current eyesight is so impaired that she can only discern blurred figures.

The legal action follows a November 11 meeting between the former first lady and her lawyers, and comes while she challenges her seven-year prison sentence handed down in January 2025 by an accountability court in the Al-Qadir Trust case. The petitioner has asked the court to summon her complete medical records, secure necessary treatment facilities, and order her transfer for eye surgery.

stories.title: Supreme Court Grants Post-Arrest Bail to Four Suspects in Placenta Smuggling Case
stories.summary:
The Supreme Court of Pakistan has granted post-arrest bail to four suspects involved in an illegal human placenta trading case. A two-member bench, headed by Justice Shahzad Ahmad Khan and including Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi, approved the bail on Monday for three Chinese nationals and one Pakistani citizen against bonds of Rs1 million each and two local sureties. The suspects were initially apprehended by the Federal Investigation Agency’s Corporate Crime Circle in Islamabad.

The arrests followed raids conducted by a joint team of the FIA and the Human Organ Transplant Authority at a residence in Sector F-7/1 and a location in Sector E-11 in Islamabad. Authorities recovered approximately 400 to 500 kilograms of fresh and dried human placentas from refrigerators at the sites. An additional export shipment weighing 580kg, misdeclared as sheep placenta and destined for Hanoi, Vietnam, was intercepted at Islamabad International Airport. In total, authorities recovered 1,241kg of human placentas linked to the network.

Deputy Attorney General Raja Shafqat Abbasi stated that the case was registered under the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 2010, along with provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code, following a complaint by HOTA medical officer Hina Kanwal. Investigators revealed the placentas were procured via a Punjab-based waste management company employee and allegedly processed for commercial export to produce anti-ageing injections. While prosecutors argued that placentas constitute human organs carrying up to 10 years of imprisonment and are a flight risk, the court observed that waste material warrants further inquiry.

This legal development matters as it addresses an underground transnational network allegedly exploiting medical waste for commercial and cosmetic gains. The illicit trade has raised serious public health concerns regarding the disposal of infectious medical waste from hospitals. Further investigations remain underway to uncover financial trails, export chains, and potential complicity of officials from customs and other departments.

stories.title: راولپنڈی: مری روڈ پر حادثے سے بچنے والا شہری نالہ لئی میں گر کر ہلاک
stories.summary:
راولپنڈی کے مصروف علاقے مری روڈ پر ایک دردناک حادثے میں بچ جانے والا معمر شہری اچانک نالہ لئی میں گر کر جاں بحق ہو گیا۔ یہ واقعہ مریڑ چوک کے قریب پیش آیا جہاں بزرگ شخص کو پہلے ہی ایک ٹریفک حادثے کا سامنا کرنا پڑا تھا، جس کے بعد راہگیروں نے اسے اٹھا کر سڑک کے کنارے بٹھا دیا تھا۔

حکام کے مطابق ابتدائی حادثے کے بعد وہ بزرگ شہری اچانک پل کے کنارے سے نیچے نالہ لئی میں جا گرا۔ حادثے کی اطلاع ملتے ہی ریسکیو ٹیمیں فوری طور پر موقع پر روانہ ہوئیں، تاہم وہ بروقت پہنچنے کے باوجود شہری کی جان نہیں بچا سکیں اور وہ پانی میں گر کر دم توڑ چکا تھا۔

ریسکیو حکام نے موقع پر پہنچ کر لاش کو نالہ لئی سے باہر نکالا۔ اس ناگہانی واقعے کے بعد علاقے میں غم و فضا پھیل گئی اور شہری انتظامیہ کے حفاظتی انتظامات پر بھی سوالات اٹھائے جانے لگے۔

اس حادثے سے متعلق قانونی کارروائی اور ضابطے کی کارروائیوں کے لیے مقامی حکام نے متعلقہ امور کی جانچ پڑتال شروع کر دی ہے تاکہ تمام حقائق کا تعین کیا جا سکے اور ضروری کارروائی عمل میں لائی جا سکے۔

stories.title: عمران خان کا اعلیٰ عدلیہ کے سربراہان کو خط، صحت سے متعلق شدید خدشات کا اظہار
stories.summary:
پاکستان تحریک انصاف کے بانی عمران خان نے چیف جسٹس آف پاکستان، چیف جسٹس وفاقی آئینی عدالت اور چیف جسٹس اسلام آباد ہائی کورٹ کے نام ایک تحریری خط ارسال کیا ہے۔ بیرسٹر سلمان صفدر کے توسط سے پہنچائے جانے والے اس خط میں بانی پی ٹی آئی نے اپنی بگڑتی ہوئی صحت پر گہرے خدشات کا اظہار کرتے ہوئے موقف اختیار کیا ہے کہ ڈاکٹروں نے انہیں برین ہیمرج اور دل کا دورہ پڑنے کے خطرے سے خبردار کیا ہے کیونکہ ان کا بلڈ پریشر 193 تک جاپہنچا ہے۔ انہوں نے استدعا کی ہے کہ عدالتی فیصلوں پر حقیقی عمل درآمد یقینی بنایا جائے کیونکہ زندہ رہنے کی صورت میں ہی وہ اپنی بے گناہی ثابت کر سکیں گے۔

دوسری جانب بانی پی ٹی آئی کی اہلیہ بشریٰ بی بی نے بھی اپنے علاج اور سرجری کے لیے اسلام آباد ہائی کورٹ میں دائر درخواست کے ذریعے رجوع کیا ہے۔ لطیف کھوسہ اور بیرسٹر سلمان صفدر کے توسط سے دائر کی گئی اس درخواست میں مؤقف اپنایا گیا ہے کہ بشریٰ بی بی کو دیکھنے میں شدید مشکلات اور آنکھ میں تکلیف کا سامنا ہے، اور 10 نومبر کو ملاقات کے دوران بانی پی ٹی آئی نے بشریٰ بی بی کی صحت کی سنگینی سے آگاہ کیا تھا۔ عدالت سے استدعا کی گئی ہے کہ ان کا مکمل طبی ریکارڈ طلب کیا جائے اور فوری طبی نگہداشت کے لیے انہیں کسی خصوصی اسپتال منتقل کرنے کے انتظامات کیے جائیں۔

مذکورہ قانونی چارہ جوئی کے دوران یہ تفصیلات بھی سامنے آئیں کہ جیل میں طبی معائنے کے بعد ڈاکٹروں نے بشریٰ بی بی کی آنکھ کی سرجری کی ضرورت ظاہر کی تھی۔ درخواست میں اس بات پر زور دیا گیا ہے کہ قیدیوں کی صحت اور طبی سہولتوں کی فراہمی پر کسی قسم کا سمجھوتہ نہیں کیا جانا چاہیے اور فوری طور پر تمام ضروری طبی امداد فراہم کی جائے۔

یہ پیشرفت ایسے وقت میں سامنے آئی ہے جب ملک بھر میں سیاسی اور عدلیہ کی سطح پر مختلف قانونی امور زیر بحث ہیں، اور پی ٹی آئی قیادت کی جانب سے جیل میں موجود رہنماؤں کی صحت اور سکیورٹی کو لے کر مسلسل تشویش کا اظہار کیا جا رہا ہے۔ عدالتوں کی جانب سے ان درخواستوں پر آئندہ سماعتوں میں مزید احکامات متوقع ہیں۔

stories.title: Finance Minister Aurangzeb Urges Banks to Increase Priority Sector Lending
stories.summary:
Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb has called upon commercial banks, including Habib Bank Limited, to expand financing for critical economic sectors. The appeal was made during a meeting in Islamabad with an HBL delegation headed by President and CEO Muhammad Nassir Salim. Discussions focused on the banking sector's vital contribution to driving economic growth, boosting investments, and widening financial inclusion across the country.

During the talks, Aurangzeb emphasized the necessity of directing funds toward priority areas such as small and medium enterprises, agriculture, housing, and electric vehicles under the Pakistan Accelerated Vehicle Electrification Scheme. He noted that robust financial institutions are essential for facilitating business transactions and providing enterprises and individuals with necessary services. The delegation also presented updates on HBL's international outreach, engagement with overseas markets, and the positive response to the Roshan Digital Account 2.0 initiative.

Furthermore, both parties explored avenues to channel long-term capital into viable infrastructure projects through enhanced private sector participation. They discussed strengthening government-HBL cooperation to position Pakistan as an appealing destination for foreign and domestic investors. Aurangzeb stressed that close coordination between state officials and banking leaders is imperative for addressing emerging economic hurdles and fostering an enabling environment for private-led growth.

This engagement is significant for shaping Pakistan's broader economic strategy and stabilizing domestic financial markets. By directing liquidity toward productive sectors, the government hopes to stimulate long-term development and improve the overall business climate. Continued collaboration between financial institutions and policymakers aims to tackle structural challenges and support sustainable economic recovery.

stories.title: Chaudhry Salik Hussain Refuses Apology or Damages in Maryam Nawaz Defamation Suit
stories.summary:
Federal Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain has formally rejected demands to apologize or pay financial damages in a defamation case filed by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz. Details of the minister's official response emerged through ARY News on Monday. The legal dispute stems from earlier corruption allegations made by Salik regarding the Punjab administration, which prompted Maryam Nawaz to issue a legal notice demanding Rs5 billion in compensation.

In his written reply, Chaudhry Salik maintained that his remarks did not provide any valid grounds for a defamation claim. He argued that his statements had been misquoted in the legal notice and categorically refused to retract his words, issue an apology, or offer monetary compensation. Furthermore, the federal minister stated his intention to present evidence of corruption before the appropriate legal and judicial forums in the future.

Salik also contended that public statements made by Maryam Nawaz herself in Jhelum validated the concerns he had initially raised regarding corruption. Additionally, he accused the Punjab chief minister of misusing public resources and the Advocate General's Office for personal legal matters. He asserted that taxpayer-funded government legal resources should not be exploited to handle private disputes.
